meta.title: Reversing Harlow's margin decline
meta.subtitle: Margin plan for the board, February 2027
meta.purpose: Approve a margin plan and its first actions
meta.confidentiality: Board discussion document; synthetic benchmark data

inputs.label: Harlow Fresh Markets briefing pack (evidence/briefing-pack.md)
inputs.content: Synthetic benchmark data: income statement FY2023–25, gross-margin drivers, store labor, shrink by labor quartile, e-commerce operating data and fee test, nine weakest stores, customer survey and competitor notes, objectives and constraints.

storyline.governing_thought: Harlow can lift operating margin to about 3.2% by FY2028 by fixing promotions, shrink and delivery pricing instead of cutting store hours across the board

exec_summary.text: Wages are not the main cause: promotions, shrink and e-commerce explain 87% of the margin fall since FY2023

sub_points.text: Operating margin fell from 3.37% to 1.02% in two years; store labor explains only 13% of it

exec_summary.text: An 8% cut in store hours would miss the target and put fresh produce at risk

sub_points.text: A shrink rise like that of FY2023–25 would erase about half of its $14.5M saving

exec_summary.text: Promotions are the largest lever, worth 0.7 percentage points of margin

sub_points.text: Returning to 24% of sales needs cuts only among the 38% of events that lose money

exec_summary.text: Home delivery lost about $10M in FY2025; the tested pricing keeps the service and saves about $2.5M a year

sub_points.text: The team's 6.1% margin leaves out delivery costs and counts every online sale as new

exec_summary.text: Five moves reach about 3.2% by FY2028, and the three that need no capital come first to clear the covenant

sub_points.text: The 2027 minimum-wage rise, up to $7.3M a year, is the main risk to the plan

next_steps.action: Stop the money-losing promotional events and cap promotions at 24% of sales; reopen vendor-funding talks
Roll out the tested delivery fee ($7.99, free above $100) to all stores and negotiate the 3% rate rise
Replace the 8% across-the-board cut with fixed fresh and receiving routines and a trim in the best-staffed quarter
Give notice on the six stores whose leases end by 2027; bring the other three to a board vote
Cost every move against the $25M cap and report monthly against the $20M covenant

sections.title: The plan and what comes first

lead_message.text: Promotions, shrink and e-commerce fulfillment, not wages, explain 87% of the fall in operating margin since FY2023

slides.rationale: What adds up to the margin change FY2023 -> FY2025 -> waterfall
slides.unit_line: **Operating margin**, % of sales, FY2023 to FY2025; steps are changes in percentage points of sales

sidebar.caption: of the fall in operating margin comes from promotions, shrink and e-commerce fulfillment
bullets: **E-commerce fulfillment:** the largest step; its cost grew 3.5 times as orders grew 2.9 times and more went to the home
**Promotions:** promotional sales earn 14 percentage points less margin, and their share of sales kept rising
**Shrink:** fresh waste, theft and receiving errors took a larger share of every sales dollar
**Store labor:** only 13% of the fall, despite being management's main explanation

footnotes: Promotions, private label and shrink account for the whole fall in gross margin; other SG&A was unchanged as a share of sales
Fiscal years end in January. Source: Harlow briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

lead_message.text: Wage inflation was largely absorbed: labor hours per dollar of sales fell 6% while the hourly wage rose 9.4%

slides.rationale: Three linked measures, three tiles -> kpi-big-numbers

items.caption: average hourly wage including benefits, FY2023 to FY2025
drivers: State minimum-wage increases and a tight labor market, as the CFO and COO say
A further 4% minimum-wage rise is due in 2027, worth up to $7.3M a year

items.caption: labor hours per $1,000 of sales, FY2023 to FY2025
drivers: Stores already run leaner than in FY2023, before any new cut
Managers in the leanest stores say produce rotation and receiving checks get skipped

items.caption: change in store labor as a share of sales
drivers: The net effect of higher wages and fewer hours per dollar of sales
Explains 13% of the fall in operating margin, not most of it

slides.unit_line: **Store labor drivers**, change FY2023 to FY2025
footnotes: Labor hours are scheduled store hours per $1,000 of sales. Source: Harlow briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

lead_message.text: Stores with the fewest labor hours lose the most to shrink, 3.1% of sales against 2.3% in the best-staffed quarter

slides.rationale: Four ordered quartiles compared on one measure -> column chart in quartile order (ranking alternative)
slides.unit_line: **Shrink**, % of sales, FY2025, stores grouped into quartiles by labor hours per $1,000 of sales

sidebar.header: Hours cut first into fresh and receiving
bullets: **Q1:** managers say produce rotation and receiving checks are skipped on busy days
**Why it bites:** fresh waste and receiving errors make up 65% of shrink, and both need staff time
**Q3 to Q4:** shrink barely moves, so the best-staffed quarter is where hours can come out safely
**Customers:** 58% shop Harlow for fresh produce, so waste also signals weaker quality
sidebar.implication: Protect fresh and receiving hours in the leanest stores; trim only the best-staffed quarter

footnotes: Stores ranked by labor hours per $1,000 of sales and split into four equal groups. Source: Harlow briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

lead_message.text: If shrink rose as it did in FY2023–25, management's hour cut would keep only about half of its $14.5M saving

slides.rationale: Our estimate of the cut's net effect, built from its parts -> calculation-bridge (B-08)

terms.caption: management's estimate of the annual saving from 8% fewer scheduled store hours
shrink rising another 0.5 percentage points of FY2025 sales, as it did when hours per $1,000 of sales fell 6%
net annual saving, 48% of the plan's figure, before any lost sales

body.assumptions_header: The estimate is cautious on four counts
assumptions: The 8% cut is deeper than the 6% fall in hours that came with the last rise in shrink
The leanest quarter of stores already loses 3.1% of sales to shrink, compared with 2.6% for the chain
Lost sales from checkout waits and stock-outs are not counted, although 44% of customers come for convenience
Even the full $14.5M would lift operating margin only to about 2.0% of FY2025 sales, short of the 3.0% target

slides.unit_line: **Annual saving from the 8% hour cut**, $ millions, FY2025 basis
footnotes: Estimate by the team from the briefing pack; live formulas in the Calculations sheet of the source workbook

lead_message.text: Promotions have grown more costly: they rose to 29% of sales while vendors funded a smaller share of markdowns

slides.rationale: Two clauses, one claim (promotions cost more) -> two panels

panels.header: Promotions now carry 29% of sales, up from 24% in FY2023
Vendors now fund less than half of each markdown dollar

slides.so_what: Each percentage point of sales moved onto promotion costs Harlow 0.14 percentage points of margin
footnotes: Promotional sales earn 14 percentage points less gross margin than regular-price sales, unchanged over the period. Source: Harlow briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

lead_message.text: Deeper promotions have not improved Harlow's price image, and customers come for fresh produce and convenience

slides.rationale: Two clauses from one survey -> two panels

panels.header: More customers call Harlow expensive than before the promotions grew
panels.unit_line: **Say Harlow is more expensive than other options**, % of respondents

panels.header: Fresh produce, not price, is the top reason to shop at Harlow
panels.unit_line: **Top reasons to shop at Harlow**, % of respondents, FY2025

footnotes: Customer survey, n = 3,100. Harlow stores near a new ValuMart: comparable sales of −4.2% in FY2025, against +1.1% elsewhere
Source: Harlow briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

lead_message.text: Cutting only money-losing events, back to 24% of sales, would add 0.7 percentage points of margin

slides.rationale: Our sizing of the promotions lever -> calculation-bridge (B-08)

terms.caption: of sales moves back to regular price, taking promotions from 29% to their FY2023 share of 24%
less gross margin on promotional sales than on regular-price sales
higher operating margin a year, about $9.9M on FY2028 sales

body.assumptions_header: Why the cut can come from losing events alone
assumptions: The 5% of sales is 17% of promotional sales, less than half of the 38% of FY2025 events that lost money even after their extra units
Sales moved off promotion stay with Harlow at regular price, and the margin gap of 14 percentage points holds
Promotions that defend traffic near ValuMart are reviewed event by event rather than cut
Not counted: recovering vendor funding from 46% toward the FY2023 level of 55% of markdowns

slides.unit_line: **Operating-margin gain from fewer promotions**, percentage points of sales, FY2028 run-rate
footnotes: The category team's case (comparable sales of +1.8% in the deepest-promotion stores, against +0.2%) measures sales, not profit
Estimate by the team from the briefing pack; live formulas in the source workbook

lead_message.text: Counted in full, e-commerce lost about $10M in FY2025, not the profit its team reports

slides.rationale: Our rebuild of e-commerce economics from its parts -> calculation-bridge (B-08)

terms.caption: contribution from the 30% of $127.8M online sales that are new to Harlow, at 20 cents a dollar
picking: $7.40 for every online order
third-party delivery: $13.80 for each of the 58% of orders delivered
delivery fees collected: $3.10 per delivered order
e-commerce result in FY2025, before any store overhead

body.assumptions_header: Two corrections turn the team's profit into a loss
assumptions: Third-party delivery is counted; the team's 6.1% margin leaves it out because finance books it in fulfillment
Only new sales count: customers say they would otherwise have bought 70% of their online purchases in a Harlow store (survey of 2,300)
Contribution of 20 cents per new dollar is finance's estimate, before fulfillment
The rebuilt fulfillment cost matches the $18.1M reported for FY2025

footnotes: Estimate by the team from the briefing pack; live formulas in the source workbook

lead_message.text: Home delivery drives the loss, with each delivered order costing $18.10 to fulfil and bringing only $5.76 of contribution

slides.rationale: Two order types compared on cost and contribution -> clustered column

series.name: Fulfillment cost per order, net of fees
Contribution from new sales per order

sidebar.header: Free delivery on most baskets makes each delivered order a loss
bullets: **Fees:** delivery is free above $75 and the average basket is $96, so most delivered orders pay no fee
**Mix:** home delivery rose from 45% to 58% of orders, so the loss grew faster than online sales
**Click-and-collect:** costs only the picking and comes close to paying for itself

rows.basis: delivered orders × (contribution − cost per order) ÷ total loss

lead_message.text: Rolling out the tested delivery pricing would cut the loss by about $2.5M a year and keep the service customers expect

drivers: About $4.4M from the six at expiry

footnotes: Four-wall EBITDA excludes depreciation and overhead, so the gain to operating income is if anything understated. Source: Harlow briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

lead_message.text: Together, five moves would lift operating margin to about 3.2% by FY2028, clearing the target before the 2027 wage rise

slides.rationale: Our plan estimate, built from the sized moves -> calculation-bridge (B-08)

terms.caption: FY2025 operating margin
promotions back to 24% of sales (0.70) and private label at its FY2023–25 pace (0.27)
store hours: fixed fresh and receiving routines in the leanest half, 8% fewer hours in the best-staffed quarter
exit of the nine loss-making stores, including the smaller sales base
delivery repriced as tested
FY2028 operating margin on $1,412M of sales

assumptions: Sales of $1,412M: FY2025's $1,503M less sales lost from store exits and the delivery test, with no market growth
Operating income rises from $15.3M to about $44.9M; the only known one-time cost is the $7.5M of lease exits
Private label keeps gaining 0.75 percentage points of sales a year at its 12 percentage-point margin premium
Not included: the 2027 minimum-wage rise, up to $7.3M if every wage rose 4%, which would leave margin near 2.7%

slides.unit_line: **Operating margin**, % of sales and percentage points, FY2025 to FY2028 run-rate
footnotes: Estimate by the team; each move is sized on its own page and in the Calculations sheet of the source workbook

lead_message.text: The five-move plan reaches the margin target that the hour cut misses, while protecting fresh and keeping home delivery

slides.rationale: Two options compared on the same criteria -> comparison-table

columns: Management draft: 8% hour cut, e-commerce frozen

cells.text: About 2.0%: $15.3M plus the full $14.5M saving, on FY2025 sales
Met if the full saving lands in FY2026
Met if the first three moves deliver a quarter of their run-rate
Cuts hours in the leanest stores too, where shrink is already 3.1%
Fixes fresh routines in the leanest half; trims only the best-staffed quarter
Frozen at today's size; still loses about $10M a year
Kept and repriced as tested; loss falls by $2.5M
Shrink and service erode half the saving
Wage rise of up to $7.3M; ValuMart's response to fewer promotions

callout.detail: Labor explains 13% of the fall; the plan works on the other 87%

footnotes: Margins are team estimates (pages 8 and 19). Source: Harlow briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data)

lead_message.text: Promotions, delivery pricing and store hours go first because they need no capital and can clear the FY2026 covenant

slides.rationale: Moves over time with decision points -> timeline-roadmap
slides.unit_line: **Plan roadmap**, by fiscal half-year, FY2026 to FY2028
slides.so_what: A quarter of the first three moves' $19.2M run-rate in FY2026 clears the $20M covenant
footnotes: Timing follows the briefing pack, which treats FY2026 as the first plan year. Estimates by the team
